{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Corio / Commerce One)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio) 
**Re:** Contract review findings and proposed redlines

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. On balance the risk allocation is workable: the vendor IP indemnity in Section 8 is one-way in our favour and uncapped (Section 9 carves it out of both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion), and the Agreement imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-volume commitment or liquidated damages on us. Auto-renewal (12-month renewals, 30-day mutual notice) and the California law/San Francisco AAA forum are acceptable, the latter at the fallback.

Six items require action. Three are critical or high and, on our reading, sit in walk-away territory or fail the fallback on material terms: (i) the Section 13.5 carve-out that transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back; (ii) the absence of any mid-term termination-for-convenience right across a five-year committed term; and (iii) the absence of any vendor insurance covenant. In addition, the Section 9 cap is measured by amounts actually paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to" rather than 12 months' fees, and carves out only Section 8 — with nothing for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The Section 2 licences run to Corio alone ("Affiliate" appears nowhere), and the Section 7.3 warranty runs only 60 days from the Effective Date with a 31 December 1999 sunset, so it can expire on or before acceptance. The Agreement also has no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation, which matters because Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service. Assignment consent (Section 14.1) needs only a reasonableness standard and an affiliate carve-out.

One item — non-solicitation — could not be verified and is carried as needs review pending sight of the separately executed NDA and Statement of Work referenced in Section 14.10.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 INDEMNIFICATION. | One-way vendor IP indemnity in our favour with standard defence procedure; uncapped via the Section 9 carve-out, so better than the fallback super-cap. No redline. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. | Section 13.5 correctly vests Corio-created Developments in Corio, but the carve-out gives Commerce One all ownership where it supports a Development on an ongoing basis, with no licence back. Walk-away territory; fails the fallback. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. | Cap is limited to amounts actually paid for the related transaction rather than 12 months' fees, and the sole carve-out is Section 8 (which runs only in our favour); no carve-out for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. | Grants are perpetual and irrevocable and survive an M&A transfer under Section 14.1, but run to Corio only — "Affiliate" appears nowhere and 2.2 is limited to Corio's internal business operations. Fails the fallback affiliate limb. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | Five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals; exits are limited to non-renewal and breach/insolvency. No customer convenience right — walk-away territory. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | SALES AND MARKETING COOPERATION | No sole-supplier or exclusive-dealing obligation on Corio; licences are non-exclusive and Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. | Section 2.7 restricts only copying and reverse engineering; Section 13.6 preserves independent development. Preferred position. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | No penalty, early-termination fee or minimum payment on us; the Section 4.4 shortfall is a true-up and the >5% trigger shifts only actual examination cost. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER. | Conformance and no-malicious-code warranties with a real remedy ladder, but only 60 days from the Effective Date with a 31 December 1999 sunset — below the 90-day fallback and capable of expiring on or before acceptance. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | Section 11.3 run-off and Section 12 escrow are useful, but there is no transition-assistance right and no data return/export obligation beyond return-or-destroy of Confidential Information. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review | § 10 CONFIDENTIALITY. | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binds Corio in this document. Verification did not pass: the separately executed NDA and Statement of Work incorporated by Section 14.10 are not before us. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 4 FEES. | Section 4.4 meets the preferred position (annual cap, reasonable time and notice, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, vendor cost absent >5% underpayment, books and records only). |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | California law, San Francisco County forum, domestic AAA seat — at the fallback, not the counterparty's home foreign forum. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 4 FEES. | No MFN, price-matching or no-less-favourable obligation anywhere; fees are fixed negotiated figures. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | PRICING | No minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty; revenue share is on actual revenue and Exhibit B sets Software Users at "Unlimited". |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | Twelve-month renewals with a mutual 30-day notice window (preferred position); Exhibit B fixes fees for Year 2–5 and beyond. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | Mutual, with an M&A carve-out and no change-of-control trigger, but consent is at absolute discretion with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate carve-out. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | No insurance clause; the only use of "insurance" is in the revenue definition. Commerce One hosts the Service and handles Corio and Customer data. Walk-away territory. |

## Walk-away items

The following are identified in our findings as walk-away territory and should be resolved before signature:

1. **Section 13.5 ownership carve-out (IP).** Transferring ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One wherever it provides ongoing support, with no licence back, is an effective transfer of our own hosting-integration IP. Our redline deletes only the carve-out, leaving Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software untouched.
2. **No termination for convenience (T4C).** A five-year committed term with no mid-term customer exit. We propose a new Section 11.2 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no penalty; 60 days' notice is available as a fallback.
3. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE).** We propose a new Section 14.10 (Insurance): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in the comment.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redlines** on the six action items: Section 13.5 (delete the ownership carve-out); Section 9 (mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, plus Excluded Claims for indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmation that fee obligations are not capped damages); Section 2 (extend the 2.1 and 2.2 licences to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, with an Affiliate definition); Section 11 (convenience termination and new Section 11.4 transition assistance up to six months at then-current rates, data return within 30 days in machine-readable format, deletion with written certification, carved back for surviving and legal-retention obligations); Section 7.3 (warranty of 12 months from acceptance, fallback 90 days from acceptance); Section 14.1 (reasonableness standard plus affiliate carve-out); and the new insurance covenant.
2. **Close the non-solicit diligence point.** Obtain the NDA and Statement of Work incorporated by Section 14.10 and confirm neither contains a non-solicit. If one is later proposed, our fallback is a mutual 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
3. **Flag the engrossing point.** Ask counterparty to delete the duplicated/garbled text at p0092 in Section 9 as a scrivener's error.
4. **Hold in reserve, to raise only if the relevant clause reopens:** an express Customer Data / hosted customer data ownership statement and the unresolved ownership of Software enhancements in the final sentence of Section 13.5; a quantified audit notice period in Section 4.4; and a renewal reminder and price-uplift cap in Section 11.1. We are not spending negotiating capital on these, nor on the indemnity sub-elements (law, data, gross negligence, "paid or payable"), given the uncapped IP indemnity and absence of any reciprocal indemnity from us."}
